sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy remains the undisputed market leader with near-perfect momentum, while a sharp rotation is underway as Basic Materials surges and Financials and Consumer Defensives lose ground.

US equity sectors are showing polarized behavior as of July 24, 2026. Energy continues to dominate the leaderboard with an exceptional momentum score of 0.933, fronting a group of four "all-green" sectors that are positive across all major timeframes (weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD). Meanwhile, Technology and Real Estate maintain strong momentum profiles, keeping them firmly in the upper echelon of the market.

In contrast, rotational shifts are actively reshaping the mid-tier. Basic Materials has emerged as a rapid mover, jumping three ranks over the last five sessions, while Utilities ticked up one spot. This upward movement comes at the direct expense of Financials and Consumer Defensives, both of which fell two spots in the rankings. Under the surface, Consumer Cyclicals and Communication Services remain heavily depressed, anchored at the bottom of the momentum ladder.

## Strength
* **Healthy Breadth:** Four out of 11 industry groups are currently "all-green," showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy is the clear market leader, holding the number one YTD rank with a dominant momentum score of 0.933.
* **Resilient Pillars:** Real Estate (momentum 0.633, rank 3) and Healthcare (momentum 0.617, rank 9) join Energy and Financials (momentum 0.567) in the all-green strength category.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Basic Materials Surging:** Basic Materials is the week's top gainer, climbing 3 spots to land at rank 5, despite a moderate momentum score of 0.483.
* **Financials and Defensives Slipping:** Financials (rank 8, momentum 0.567) and Consumer Defensive (rank 7, momentum 0.300) are the biggest losers over the last five sessions, both dropping 2 spots.
* **Technology Holding High Ground:** Technology is the second-strongest momentum leader at 0.700, maintaining its YTD rank of 2.
* **Persistent Laggards:** Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.067, rank 11) and Communication Services (momentum 0.150, rank 10) continue to show severe relative weakness.

## Divergences
* **Basic Materials Early-Warning:** Basic Materials exhibits an emerging divergence, with its rank jumping 3 spots in 5 days to rank 5, even though its overall momentum score remains low at 0.48.
* **Fragile Healthcare Green:** Healthcare is flagged as a fragile all-green sector; despite its positive performance across all timeframes, a low agreement score of 0.44 points to an unstable rank.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive and industrial themes like Healthcare REITs and Railroads anchor a bifurcated market, while metals emerge and internet-related groups face sharp corrections.

Market leadership remains concentrated in defensive and heavy industrials, with 25 of 144 groups maintaining all-green status across all timeframes. REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.91 momentum) and Railroads (0.88 momentum) anchor this strength, alongside sustained performance in Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing. Meanwhile, a clear rotation is underway into metals and resources, with Silver (+18 spots), Aluminum (+16 spots), and Copper (+12 spots) surging in rank over the last five sessions.

Conversely, consumer and digital-facing groups are fading rapidly. Internet Content & Information collapsed by 31 spots to rank 99, while Internet Retail dropped 16 spots. High-momentum areas are also showing vulnerability; Staffing & Employment Services dropped 12 spots despite a 0.68 momentum score, signaling that some previously resilient trends are starting to fracture.

## Strength
* **All-Green Breadth:** 25 out of 144 industry groups are positive across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, YTD), led by REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.91 momentum), Railroads (0.88 momentum), and Financial Conglomerates (0.88 momentum).
* **Sustained Leaders:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.88 momentum) and Banks - Diversified continue to show deep structural strength, remaining top-ranked across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Industrial Resilience:** Marine Shipping (0.87 momentum) and Steel (0.85 momentum) reinforce the persistent bid for physical trade and infrastructure-linked sectors.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Conglomerates jumped 20 spots to rank 58 (0.67 momentum), followed closely by Silver (+18 spots to rank 77) and Aluminum (+16 spots to rank 80).
* **Severe Decliners:** Internet Content & Information fell 31 spots to rank 99 (0.31 momentum), alongside Internet Retail which slid 16 spots to rank 105.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Mortgage Finance (0.05 momentum, rank 142) and Auto Manufacturers (0.08 momentum, rank 139) remain deeply depressed at the bottom of the YTD rankings.

## Divergences
* **Emerging Metals & Resources:** Aluminum (+16 spots, 0.42 momentum), Gold (+10 spots, 0.40 momentum), and Uranium (+7 spots, 0.26 momentum) are rapidly climbing the rankings despite currently low absolute momentum scores.
* **Fading High-Flyers:** Staffing & Employment Services (0.68 momentum, -12 spots) and Consumer Electronics (0.83 momentum, -6 spots) are showing early fatigue as their rankings slip despite strong historical momentum.
* **Defensive Rotation:** Utilities - Independent Power Producers jumped 12 spots to rank 124, showing early signs of accumulation despite a modest 0.38 momentum score.
